note: The lanes, priorities, and actor-grouped transition allow-list for a localswim board. User definitions live in each board JSON. Under edges, each actor id maps to permitted directed edges with required from and to fields and an optional description. Schema 6 introduced this grouping and renamed the former edge note field to description.

lanes.label: Backlog
lanes.note: Work Terry has explicitly held back, work that is not yet scoped well enough for Bot to perform, and optional umbrella cards that organize executable child cards.

lanes.label: Ready For Work
lanes.note: Work scoped well enough for Bot to perform, ordered by priority. Dependencies on other Ready For Work cards affect execution order, not readiness.

lanes.label: In progress
lanes.note: The one card Bot is actively performing.

lanes.label: Blocked
lanes.note: Neither Bot nor Terry can act until an external condition changes, such as hardware arriving from a vendor. Do not use this lane for dependencies on other board cards.

lanes.label: Needs Terry
lanes.note: Bot work waiting for Terry to answer, approve a recommendation, make a judgment call, or personally act.

lanes.label: Ready for review
lanes.note: Bot believes the work is complete and awaits Terry's review; Bot may not sign off its own work.

lanes.label: Completed
lanes.note: Work Terry reviewed and accepted. Terminal because no transition leaves this lane.

terry.description: Promotion means Bot has enough scope to perform the card. Terry may promote it directly; under the current Terry workflow, Bot also triages every sufficiently scoped backlog card without per-ticket permission. Dependencies on other Ready For Work cards affect execution order, not readiness.
Terry may start a backlog card directly. Bot has no direct edge and promotes sufficiently scoped Bot work to Ready For Work before starting it.

Terry pulling one of his own someday cards forward as a REMINDER TO HIMSELF. Terry, 2026-08-19: "add a state machine perms rule to allow terry to move from Backlog to Needs Terry... Trying to leave myself a reminder." The lane note frames this lane as "Claude is STOPPED until Terry answers", and this row widens it by one reading: Needs Terry is the only lane the title bar counts as HIS call to action, so it is where a thing he must personally do belongs, whether or not Claude waits on it. It grants no power he lacked -- he already owned backlog->ready_for_work and backlog->in_progress -- it grants the honest destination.

Claude may push a card BACKWARDS. Terry, 2026-08-19: "yes claude can push backwards from RFW to backlog. In progress to Backlog or RFW. from blocked to any swimlane left of it. from needs terry to any lane left of it." Setting work down is not advancing a queue, which is what the forward edges guard.

Terry may drag selected work from Ready For Work to In progress when he starts it. Terry requested this browser permission explicitly on 2026-08-22. Ownership remains a label and does not grant or restrict the edge.

bot.description: Promotion means Bot has enough scope to perform the card. Terry delegates backlog triage and work ordering to Bot, so Bot promotes every sufficiently scoped card without per-ticket permission. Dependencies on other Ready For Work cards affect execution order, not readiness.

Claude may take a backlog card to Needs Terry and NOWHERE else. Terry, 2026-08-18: "that way if I comment in backlog, you can reply with a clarify question and move it to Needs Terry."
